chapter: Pay, the Fletcher Henderson circle and later life
title: Running the changes versus creating on a solo
summary: Caldwell tells students not to just run notes and says he creates as he goes, never repeating a solo.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: That's right. He's correct. He's correct. I heard him -- it's a funny thing, you know, I don't like to criticize people, but I always listened to what -- these guys, to what they play. Over where I work at the (unintelligible) over (unintelligible) there for different groups take a group over there probably next month come in so I could (unintelligible) in the school and all. This curriculum there, very nice, and all these fellows wanted to run. So when they got -- they asked me a question, I said -- oh, they asked you a question. That's playing very nice -- criticizing, you know. I said, for instance, a man come up and asked you to give you your rendition of "Body and Soul", "I Cover the Waterfront", some number, (unintelligible), you don't run. (to have) You got the tone and the expression. So that's all they're doing is running.

I said, that's good. But, you know, when (unintelligible) it says Fast when you run two things, you run out of music. I said, now, when you're going to play six, seven different choruses courses, you're not running, you got to concentrate as you go. Now, when they wrote that article about me, I didn't

know that they were going to write that article because I have no idea Johnny Simmen didn't (unintelligible) was going to put it in a book. I just wanted to it (unintelligible) played because I wanted to play, and I choruses up the horn didn't have no kind of courses. I'd never take a run, like when I practiced at home. I'd do scales and chords, play three, four bars of this and that, but sit down and just concentrate, I'm going to play 99 choruses, uh-uh.

But when he took that story down, all I was playing, just what's coming to my mind, because I create as I go, see. The feeling is going to -- it works up, and I create as I go. If you'd ask me what did you play yesterday on that nine choruses you're taking because (unintelligible) -- consecutive chorus, I'd say, well, I couldn't tell you unless you taped it.
I wouldn't have gotten, wouldn't have played the same thing again anyway.
No, it's the way you feel.
